statement: The first line holds a string s of uppercase letters; the second holds k. You may change at most k characters. Print the length of the longest substring you can turn into one repeated letter. A window is feasible when its length minus the count of its most frequent letter is at most k - that difference is the number of changes needed. Grow the right end, maintain per-letter counts and the running top count, and advance the left end when the window turns infeasible.

example.why: Change the lone B in AABA or the lone A in ABBA - either way four equal letters stand in a row.

hint: Length minus top frequency is the repair bill; the window is legal while the bill is at most k.
mistake: Fearing the stale top count after shrinking - it only makes the check stricter and the answer stays right.
